JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.3,50,000/- for the damages suffered to the Petitioner's Hyundai Eon Era Car bearing No.KA-02-MH-3426 in a road accident dated 09.10.2021.
2.
The case of the Petitioner in brief is as follows:-

That on 09.10.2021 at about 08.30pm, the petitioner was driving her Hyundai Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MH- 3426 on Tumakuru-Bengaluru NH-4 Road, from PS Junction towards Jalahalli Cross Junction, following all the traffic rules in a correct side of the road slowly and carefully, a TATA LPT Goods vehicle/Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-7049 came with high speed, without following any traffic rules and regulations, so as to endangering human life, all of a sudden came in the same direction from back side of the petitioner's car and dashed the right rear side of the petitioner's Car, when the Car turned, the said Lorry dashed to the right side driving portion of the Car thereby the Car damaged.
After MVA inspection, the petitioner shifted her damaged Car to RM Motors, Nelagadaranahalli Main Road, Nagasandra Post, Rukmini Nagar, Bangalore and got repaired the same.

So far the petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards replacement of damaged parts, tinkering, labor charges,
parking charges and other incidental expenses.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, she and her family members were using the Car for daily routine work.

Due to the said accident and extensive damage, the petitioner has left her Car for repair and hence she used hire the vehicles/cabs for her and her family members daily routine work and spending Rs.2,000/- per day thereby, she has incurred huge loss.

Further the value of the Car is also reduced considerably owing to the damaged caused to the Car on account of the accident thereby the petitioner is undergoing great mental shock, agony and pecuniary loss.
The accident is solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the TATA LPT Goods vehicle/Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-7049.
In this connection the jurisdictional Peenya Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.0134/2021 p/u/Sec.279 of IPC against the driver of the said TATA LPT Goods vehicle/Lorry.
The Respondents being the RC owner and insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
4. In response to the notice issued by this Tribunal, the respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this court Nasreen Taj vs Maheshwari .P

2 hence, placed ex-parte.
5.

The written statement of the respondent No.2 is as follows:
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy to the TATA LPT Goods vehicle/Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-7094 in favour of the Respondent No.1.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid driving license as on the date of accident.
Further stated that the offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit and fitness certificate.
Further denied that the ownership of the Respondent No.1.
Further denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
The accident occurred only on account of the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MH-3426.
The accident was not occurred on account of the rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle.
It has denied the manner of accident.
It has also denied the expenses made by the petitioner towards damage of her Car in the accident.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following Issues:-
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 09-10-2021 at 8:00pm due to rash and negligent driving of driver of TATA LPT goods vehicle/Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-7049 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7. The Petitioner in order to prove her case, has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.
On the other side the Respondent No.2 did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.

8. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for both the parties and perused the materials on record.
9.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on records this court answers the above issues as follows:-
Issue No.1: Partly in the affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:-

sentences.text: 3 REASONS 10. Issue No.1: The Petitioner to prove that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of the part of the driver of the offending TATA LPT Goods vehicle/Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-7049 has examined herself as PW.1 and produced 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.
She has reiterated the contents of the petition in her affidavit filed in lieu of her chief examination.
She has also produced documents such as FIR in Cr. No.134/2021 of Peenya Traffic Police with complaint, spot mahazar with spot sketch, IMV report and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.4.
The contents of complaint is herewith reproduced for better appreciation:
On careful reading of the complaint, it can be gathered that the Lorry driver driven his vehicle by consuming alcohol and dashed to the rear side of complainant's Car.
Again the offending Lorry dashed to the Driving side of the Car.
Hence, it is not safe to hold that the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the offending TATA LPT Goods vehicle.
In deed, the charge sheet has filed against the driver of the offending TATA LPT Goods vehicle.
11. The First Information Statement indicates that the complaint has lodged on 12.10.2021 at about 12.45pm against to accident occurred on 09.10.2021 at about 08:00pm.
The police have not taken any pain to make reference about delay in lodging the complaint in the FIR.
At this juncture, it is Nasreen Taj vs Maheshwari .P

4 beneficial to refer the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of RAVI V/s.
BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that "in accident cases,
human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim cannot be dismissed merely on that ground although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases.
Delay in lodging the claim should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to 1(2011) 4 SCC 693 demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof."
12. In the light of the Judgment referred to supra in RAVI's case, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof.

It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.4, this Tribunal is of view that the accident has not occurred sole negligent act of the driver of the offending TATA LPT Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA-52- 7049.
Accordingly Issue No.1 held partly in affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
The petitioner ought to prove the expenses incurred to the repair of the car and also damages occurred in the alleged accident.
The petitioner has totally relied on Motor Vehicle Inspection Report marked at Ex.P3 to substantiate the damages occurred to her vehicle.
On careful scrutiny of this document the petitioner's Car was got damaged more than the offending Lorry.

The vehicle of the petitioner's viz.,
KA-02-MH-3426 has got damaged to its right hand side both doors pressed inward and jammed and damaged.
Front right side door glass broken and damaged.
Front right side body, above wheel windguard body pressed and damaged.
Rear side corner (Right) body also pressed and damaged.

Per contra the offending vehicle i.e., TATA LPT Goods vehicle/Lorry bearing No.KA-52-7049 has got damaged to its front side bumper body slightly scratched and fresh rubbing scraches found on front side,
number plate and also on bumper body.
It shows that the the offending vehicle hit the right side of the Car.

sentences.text: The Petitioner has reiterated the petition averments in the evidence led as PW.1 with regard to the damages caused to her vehicle and repair cost.
The Petitioner by producing the IMV report at Ex.P.3 has proved that her vehicle bearing No.KA-02-MH-3426 got damaged in the accident.
Apart from this, the Petitioner has produced Tax Invoices at Ex.P.8 issued by Shri Raam Automobiles for a sum of Rs.22,974/- (repair Estimation) and Rs.29,028/- tinkering and painting charges.
To prove the same the petitioner has not examined the author of this document or witness of this document.

During the cross examination of PW.1, she has stated that at the time of repair of the Car, she has spent daily Rs.2,000/- towards her travel expenses but she has not produced any bills/document to show the same.
On careful perusal of the Invoice summary, the vehicle was got repaired tinkering and painting.
These documents does not discloses mode of payment.
The petitioner has not produced any piece of document to shows the mode of payment.
Hence, it is appears to the tribunal that the petitioner has produced these bills without any payment receipt.

Hence, by considering parts of the vehicle and cost of repairing, the petitioner is entitled for a compensation amount of Rs.50.000/-.
15.
Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the Petitioner has proved the existence of insurance policy, the Respondent No.2 - insurer has to indemnify the Respondent No.1.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.3,50,000/-.
But she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.50,000/- along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER

The petition is allowed in part The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondent No.2 insurer of the  offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
